I will try to instruct you from the beginning as best I can in the fewest words
586 ⟦1⟧ 198. 436. So with this the stichomythia is indicated, which here too, as at 198. 415, is introduced with three verses.

- 588 ⟦1⟧’ is inappropriate; ⟦2⟧’ is correct (⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧). On 589 cf. schol.; hence ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧. ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧. Also Plato Phaedr. 256 B (Paley): ⟦9⟧. 590. The dative as with ⟦10⟧. 591: according to the scholiast, by ⟦11⟧ the motives are meant, and Orestes misunderstands; but ⟦12⟧ quite unambiguously denotes the manner of the murder, on which something also depended, cf. 629 ff. — 592 Orestes answers unshaken and confident, as he behaves throughout the drama. The expression ⟦13⟧ is somewhat peculiar, but Homeric ⟦14⟧ (Δ 108) and the like offer ample comparison. 595 “Incredible! The ⟦15⟧ (169) and ⟦16⟧ of holy law commands this?” ⟦17⟧ also stands at 609; ⟦18⟧ ⟦19⟧.

cutting with his hand at the throat

for this god, I suppose, is the ancestral expounder for all men in such matters, seated at the navel of the earth, and he expounds

Harpocration ⟦8⟧ (Stanley). “I have not fared badly, but am still safe.” 601 ⟦9⟧ for ⟦10⟧ is restored according to the scholiast. With this Orestes brings the second point of his justification (again at 605): I had to avenge my father.

he brought evil upon the city

— 604 Schol. ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, and of course in ⟦4⟧ lies that the chorus does not care what Clytemnestra has done. With 605 now Orestes brings also the third point of his justification: Clytemnestra was a husband-murderer, which is no less bad than mother-murder, see the discussion between Apollo and the Erinyes 211 ff.
